title: Hybrid SSE/WebSocket compatibility adapter with progressive checksum reassembly
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a compatibility adapter that allows clients to receive streaming model outputs over both SSE and WebSocket transports while preserving function/tool-call boundaries and enabling incremental JSON reassembly with progressive checksums. This ticket covers protocol framing, checksum strategy, reconnect/resume semantics, client-side reassembly hints, and server-side backpressure signals. Motivation: a subset of customers operate through proxies or environments that prefer WebSocket while others rely on SSE; we must provide a single server-side behavior that guarantees deterministic tool-call boundaries and structured output even across reconnects or mixed-transport fallbacks.

Scope:
- Define wire framing markers for chunk-level metadata (sequence id, fragment index, semantic boundary flags, progressive checksum).
- Implement server encoder that emits the framing envelope for both SSE and WebSocket paths.
- Implement resume token semantics that include checksum and last-accepted-sequence for safe reconnection and cross-transport resume (e.g., client connects via SSE, fails, reconnects via WS).
- Add client-facing heuristics: reassembly timeout, partial-JSON acceptance policy, and strict tool-call atomicity configuration.
- Integrate with function/tool calling logic to avoid split tool payloads across reassembly boundaries unless explicitly allowed.

Non-goals: full transport-level reliability layer (we rely on existing TLS/TCP), heavyweight multi-node checkpoint store (we'll use ephemeral in-memory resume windows with optional durable store later).
acceptance_criteria: Server emits framed chunks over SSE and WS with identical chunk metadata schema
Client can resume a stream on the other transport using resume token and reach same reconstructed output or fail with explicit mismatch error
Tool/function call payloads are never split across reassembled toolcall JSON objects unless opt-in flag is enabled
Progressive checksum allows server and client to detect incompatible partial-history within 1-2 chunks
End-to-end integration tests for reconnect, transport-fallback, and malformed-chunk handling are added to CI
implementation_notes: Framing envelope fields: seq (monotonic per-session), frag_idx (0-based), boundary_type (none|semantic|toolcall|final), checksum_prefix (sha256 hex truncated 12), metadata_jsonlen (optional)
Resume token = base64(session_id + ':' + last_seq + ':' + checksum_prefix) so clients can attempt cross-transport resume without exposing full history

On reconnect: server validates resume token against active resume window. If token checksum mismatch -> respond with resume_reject error including suggested fallback: full-restart or canonical-checkpoint URL
Backpressure: add 'x-riq-credit' SSE comment / WS control message to indicate client-targeted pacing hints; not a hard quota but advisory for autoscaling tuning

Tool-calling safety: runtime must buffer up to a configurable limit (default 256KB) to ensure toolcall JSON is complete before emitting a toolcall boundary flag; if exceeded, emit a 'toolcall-split-warning' in chunk metadata and set boundary_type=semantics_repair
Telemetry: instrument chunk-level metrics (emit_rate, avg_fragment_size, resume_success_rate, cross_transport_resume_mismatch) and expose in Console under per-model streaming tab
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Drafted protocol envelope. Shared initial proposal doc: docs/streaming/hybrid-framing-proposal.md. Asked infra for readiness to add resume window state to the ingress layer.

2026-03-04 - Marco Delgado: POC encoder implemented for SSE path. Verified sequence and frag_idx on local harness. Observed 0.3% checksum collision rate on synthetic fuzz (expected due to truncated prefix) — will increase prefix length to 12 hex chars to reduce false positives.

2026-03-06 - SRE (review): Raised concern that resume windows retained in memory across many concurrent sessions could increase memory pressure. Suggested LRU eviction strategy and per-tenant cap. Added to implementation notes.

2026-03-08 - PM (Janelle Wong): Confirmed requirement to never split toolcall payloads by default; added label and acceptance criteria. Prioritizing for enterprise customers running private deployments.
2026-03-09 - Marco Delgado: Started WS adapter and cross-transport resume unit tests. Noted an edge case where proxies translate SSE comments; added alternative control-frame for pure-WS clients.
2026-03-10 - Design (Liu Chen): Reviewed chunk metadata UX for Console; requested human-readable boundary names and a 'reassembly diagnostics' panel. Filing follow-up design ticket in design lane.
